learnings.title: REST API writes obey GitHub push rulesets; preserve append-only archive writer
learnings.claim: GitHub push rulesets can restrict file paths and also apply to REST API create blob, create tree, and create or update file contents endpoints; private/internal push rulesets require an eligible plan and can block legitimate append writers without a tested bypass.
learnings.decision: ARCHIVE_REST_PUSH_RULESET_GATE: Before enabling archive path restrictions, check repo plan/visibility and permissions; stage ruleset in evaluate mode, test that a prohibited full overwrite is blocked and authorized append remains possible, and only then consider enforcement. Until live proof, preserve existing append-only guards, compare blob SHA, and read back length/prefix after every write. Never assume CI alone blocks direct API overwrite.
learnings.next_measurement: Grok: identify actual repo rulesets/plan and archive writer identity; add negative test for REST Contents overwrite plus positive append; capture run ID, response code and unchanged archive SHA/length; if push ruleset unsupported, document code-level fail-closed alternative.
failure_history: 2026-10-10 prior archive truncations to SEE_FILE / placeholder were reported and repaired; repo-level API enforcement remains unverified.
fallback_history: Do not enable a blocking ruleset without proving the legitimate append-only writer is not interrupted; keep existing archive-heal and CI guards as partial protection.
